levers.name: LR_STEPS
levers.effect: Sets the cosine wavelength in STEPS rather than deriving it from LR_EPOCHS. 0 = derive from LR_EPOCHS. Set to 280000 for round16 (matching what sched_ctl's 8 epochs actually spanned), 260000 for lr_075_short, 90000 for lr_075_rst.

levers.name: LR_RESTARTS
levers.effect: Whether the cosine wraps into repeated cycles. LR_RESTARTS=0 forces `_p = min(1.0, _prog); _n, _ci = 1, 0`, which makes BOTH LR_RESTART_DAMP and LR_DECAY structurally unreachable.

levers.name: LR_RESTART_DAMP
levers.effect: NEW in this range, default 0.5. Each cycle records the best held-out it inherited; a cycle that fails to beat it halves the next restart's swing, cumulatively. Cannot reach cycle 1 at all.

levers.name: LR_DECAY
levers.effect: A decaying envelope over restart cycles. Pre-existing but shipped at 0.0 (off) since it was written; flipped to default 1.0 in this range and gated on `_n > 1` so it is an exact no-op on any single-cycle schedule. Ungated it squeezed single-cycle runs too, ending them at LR_MIN_FRAC squared.

levers.name: LR_SHIFT_WARM
levers.effect: Re-warms the LR after an epoch resample, as an attenuation of the cycle. Left at 0 (off): none of round15's worst excursions were resample-aligned, so it acts nowhere near the instability.

levers.name: BLOWUP_RISE / BLOWUP_STALE
levers.effect: NEW module-level constants, 0.5 bits/byte and 80 probes. The divergence alarm fires only when the median of the last three probes sits >=0.5 above the best AND 80 probes have passed with no new best. Chosen because 80 gave clean separation (zero wrong) across all nine real runs.
levers.owner: blowup_stale() in self_organize.py, exercised by blowup_test.py

levers.name: CURVE_RISE_BLEWUP / CURVE_FLAT / CURVE_TOK_RISE
levers.effect: 0.5 / 0.05 / 0.05. Thresholds of the hoisted curve_verdict(), returning vocab|blewup|recovering|plateau|diverging|none.
levers.owner: curve_verdict() in self_organize.py, exercised by curve_test.py

levers.name: FAB_PRESSURE
levers.effect: 0.45. A SETPOINT, not a limit: cull_gate_open is n_live/cap >= FAB_PRESSURE, and the population equilibrates at pressure x cap. Three mechanisms live behind that gate — the utilization cull, the utilization spare, and FAB_RESCUE.

levers.name: FAB_NMAX
levers.effect: The preallocated slot pool (cap). Changing it on a resume moves the cull gate, the ramp latch, and the pressure setpoint all at once. pilot-add now sets it to double the checkpoint's cap automatically.

levers.name: FAB_N0
levers.effect: Starting population. pilot-add now reads it from the checkpoint's fab_cfg["n"] (523 in the real case) rather than taking the registry default 2048 — which would manufacture 1525 identity experts at step 0 that growth never asked for.

levers.name: GROW_CAP_FAB0
levers.effect: The soft cap the capacity valve starts from; the valve only ever lifts it. `_cap_fab = [int(_i("GROW_CAP_FAB0", 0)) or FAB_NMAX]` is rebuilt from the environment on every resume, and the clamp `_nb = min(_nb, _cap_fab[0] - fab.n())` goes NEGATIVE — freezing growth for the whole run — whenever fab.n() exceeds the soft cap.

levers.name: MANAGE_EVERY / BATCH_W
levers.effect: MANAGE_EVERY=500 default, BATCH_W=1 default (16 in the pilots, 12 in fix_cadence). The management cadence was `step % MANAGE_EVERY == 0` below the batch early-out; changed to `_nbwd % max(1, MANAGE_EVERY // max(1, BATCH_W)) == 0` at five sites so the cadence is BATCH_W-invariant.

levers.name: ACCUM
levers.effect: Gradient accumulation. Was `(step + 1) % ACCUM == 0` below the batch early-out, so at BATCH_W=16 ACCUM=4 it either fires on every flush or never for the epoch; changed to `_nbwd % ACCUM` so it counts backward passes.

levers.name: VMAX
levers.effect: The softmax width, distinct from the tokenizer's vocabulary. Under TOK_ONLINE the model is built to it and the tokenizer mints into it for the whole run. It was full at 2048 before Python arrived, so the new area got zero tokens. pilot-add now doubles it from the checkpoint via VMAX=${VMAX:-2048}.

levers.name: EXPOSURE_MAX / EXPOSURE_SKEW
levers.effect: NEW knobs (2.0 and 3.0). Whole-run guards on per-corpus repetition and per-corpus exposure imbalance. Registered next to VAL_FRAC. Fired on the real CL run as "EXPOSURE IMBALANCE 5.6x".

levers.name: MEM_WRONG_READ
levers.effect: NEW knob, default 1. Separates DETECTING a self-inconsistent memory entry from ACTING on it. Previously Memory.read filtered on the same is_wrong() predicate that WRONG_SWEEP gated, so "detect-only" excluded 63,146 genuine entries from every retrieval.

levers.name: WRITE_QUANTILE / WRITE_ADAPTIVE

levers.name: MEM_SRC_FLOOR

levers.name: MEM_PER_EXPERT / KEY_PREGATE / KEY_BATCH / KEY_SRC

carry_forward.item: A fix that lands only in code and never inside a run has not been demonstrated. round18 exists precisely to make each repair visible in a log; unit tests hold the arithmetic, only a run shows the mechanism firing inside the system.

Instrument the repair itself (mint_rescued / mint_widened / gate_skipped), not just its outcome.
carry_forward.why: This is the difference between evidence and a coincidence, and it was only caught after the run.

carry_forward.item: The correct pairing of an added-area resume: FAB_N0 = the checkpoint's live count, FAB_NMAX = DOUBLE the checkpoint's cap, VMAX = double the checkpoint's vocabulary. Not the registry defaults, and not four times anything.
carry_forward.why: 523 live in cap 1024 ended at 0.51 occupancy; cap 2048 puts a doubled 1046 back in that same regime, while cap 4096 shuts the cull gate for the whole run AND re-arms the population ramp. Registry defaults (2048/4096) crash outright or, after the widening fix, produce a number nobody can interpret.

carry_forward.item: fab_cfg records n, rank, cap, dk and the checkpoint now also carries fab_use, fab_born, fab_uage, cap_fab, and PlateauGrowth's learned state (EMAs, ramp latch, clocks, counters). Anything a resume needs must TRAVEL WITH THE CHECKPOINT, not be re-read from the environment.
carry_forward.why: Every one of those was, at some point in this range, either recorded and never read or rebuilt from env on a resume — and each produced a silent wrong answer rather than a crash. PlateauGrowth's state is the sharpest: without it, the regression trigger (the only signal continual learning has) is structurally blind at the exact moment an area arrives.

carry_forward.item: cull_gate_open is n_live/cap >= FAB_PRESSURE, and THREE mechanisms live behind it — the utilization cull, the utilization spare, and FAB_RESCUE. FAB_PRESSURE is a SETPOINT: the population equilibrates at pressure x cap. Changing the cap therefore changes what the population wants to be, not just what it may become.
carry_forward.why: A wrong answer at that gate does not fail — it silently removes three things from the run and they read ARMED AND INERT as an artefact of the cap rather than a finding. The docstring records it having already done that once.

carry_forward.item: Two preallocated geometries in this system grow by advancing a counter rather than reallocating — the fabric's expert slots (FAB_NMAX) and the softmax width (VMAX) — so a smaller checkpoint is a genuine PREFIX of a larger live model. widen_prefix() serves both. Narrowing is refused (it discards trained work); a changed FAB_RANK or FAB_DK is refused (inner dimensions).
carry_forward.why: Refusing to widen would mean a resume can never add capacity for the area it is adding, which is the whole exercise. Getting the prefix relation right is what made goal B runnable.

carry_forward.item: bits/byte is LOWER-IS-BETTER, so forgetting is LATEST MINUS EARLIEST. Any drift/BWT/retention number must use that convention, and any mean must be taken over domains that PREDATE the run — a domain that arrived this run can cancel an old domain's forgetting.
carry_forward.why: RETENTION had the subtraction inverted on the exact line the CL claim rests on, and printed DRIFTING because Python IMPROVED. bwt_of's own docstring records the same fault, in the section directly beneath it.

carry_forward.item: Anything below the batch early-out (`if len(_bx) < BATCH_W: step += 1; continue`) counts FLUSHES, not steps. Any `step % N == 0` there is a unit mismatch that fires for a minority of residues. Use `_nbwd % max(1, N // max(1, BATCH_W))`.
carry_forward.why: This was found at five sites in this range (three management cadences, then ACCUM). At BATCH_W=16 MANAGE_EVERY=500 the gate fires for 4 of 16 residues; at BATCH_W=16 ACCUM=4 the optimizer either steps every flush or NEVER for the epoch.

carry_forward.item: A budget must be sized on the set it can be SPENT on. The cull ranks within _elig (experts past the USE grace) but sized its budget on n_live.
carry_forward.why: In the only continual-learning run ever performed: n_live 523, eligible 84, budget 10 instead of 1 — a 10x over-cull aimed precisely at the population a resume exists to preserve. Nearly the whole 523 -> 448 loss is this bug.

carry_forward.item: 'Detect-only' must be checked for EVERY consumer of the flag, not just the obvious one. WRONG_SWEEP gated deletion; Memory.read filtered on the same predicate.
carry_forward.why: 63,146 genuine entries at 3% precision were excluded from every retrieval — about a third of the store — while the log read as reassurance and memory still contributed +0.085 b/B. MEM_WRONG_READ now separates the two decisions.

carry_forward.item: DN and CORP are index-aligned; open_corpus returns one entry per name in DOMAINS order. Any filter on CORP must drop the matching name. Name-keying in report_holdout stops a REORDER, not a DROP, because the name is read out of the desynced list.
carry_forward.why: An undersized first corpus makes the next run compare this run's Python against last run's English and report the difference as forgetting — the number goal B rests on, computed across two languages. And the trigger is precisely the 'corpus too small' error the owner reported.

carry_forward.item: Exposure is a WHOLE-RUN quantity. build_stream draws per corpus in PHASE_SCHED's proportions; a guard that sums the corpora, or that measures per epoch, misses the imbalance entirely. EXPOSURE_MAX=2.0 and EXPOSURE_SKEW=3.0 encode this.
carry_forward.why: 60 MB English + 8 MB Python reads as 68 MB against a 4 MB stream and passes a summed check. The real run then printed EXPOSURE IMBALANCE 5.6x: eng 0.28x, py 1.56x — a live confound on the headline continual-learning number.

carry_forward.item: PHASE_SCHED for two corpora is [[0],[0],[1],[1]] — the original area for the first half of each epoch, the added area for the second, REPEATED EVERY EPOCH. At EPOCHS=8 the original is rehearsed eight times during the run that measures what forgot it. PURE_ADD=1 is the arm the modularity claim actually rests on.
carry_forward.why: Rehearsal is a legitimate CL method, but under it 'modularity protected the old area' is not what is being measured. The owner should decide which arm they want.

carry_forward.item: A default that cannot fire is worse than one that is off: WRITE_QUANTILE=1 gated behind WRITE_ADAPTIVE=0; TOK_ANCHOR=0.05 whose loss term never enters the loss; LR_DECAY/LR_RESTART_DAMP unreachable on every arm that would be run. carry_forward.why: 'Armed and inert' is the project's core discipline, and the audit built to catch it was itself blind to the LR schedule (20 rows, none about the learning rate) and to is_wrong() (which gates every memory retrieval).
